name: seam-debugger
description: Mixed-mode debugging for Python programs with C, C++ and Rust extensions on Linux: one call stack, breakpoints and stepping across the boundary.

seam.adapterCommand.description: Command that starts the Seam debug adapter. Change it if `seam` is not on PATH, e.g. ["/path/to/venv/bin/seam", "dap"].

seam.logFile.description: If set, the adapter writes a protocol log to this file (for bug reports).

module.description: Python module to run with -m (instead of program).

args.description: Arguments for the script or module.

python.description: Python interpreter (3.12 or newer). A name is looked up on PATH.

pythonArgs.description: Arguments for the interpreter itself, before the script.

enumDescriptions: Run the program in VS Code's integrated terminal. It can read from the keyboard.
Show the program's output in the Debug Console. The program cannot read input.
Run the program in an external terminal window.
console.description: Where the program's input and output go.

stopOnEntry.description: Stop on the first line of Python code.

stopOnSignals.description: Signals that stop the debugger. Every other signal is delivered to the program without stopping.

justMyCode.description: For the "Raised Python exceptions" breakpoint: ignore exceptions that stay inside the standard library and installed packages.

debugInfoLookup.description: Let LLDB look for separate debug-info files for system libraries.

showGlueFrames.description: Show binding-layer trampoline frames (pybind11, PyO3, ...) in the call stack.

frameworkPaths.description: Extra path fragments marking native source files as glue to step through, e.g. "/third_party/".

pid.description: Process id of a running CPython 3.12+ process.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the process to reach a point where the helper can load.

configurationSnippets.description: Attach to a running Python process by pid.
